title: Neural Topic Modeling with Large Language Models in the Loop
subcategory: LLM-in-the-loop refinement of neural topic models
task: Topic discovery on long and short document collections
problem: Direct LLM topic discovery suffers from incomplete topic coverage, topic misalignment and inefficiency, while NTM topics are often hard to interpret.
architecture: Plug-in framework (LLM-ITL) on top of an existing NTM: the NTM learns global topics and document-topic representations; an LLM prompted with each topic's top words (chain-of-thought prompt) returns a topic label and refined topic words; an Optimal Transport distance aligns the NTM topic-word distribution with the LLM-refined words; the alignment loss is weighted by the LLM's confidence (label token probability or word-intrusion confidence); refinement starts after a warm-up phase.
llm_or_encoder: LLaMA3-8B-Instruct (main experiments); GloVe word embeddings build the OT cost matrix
metrics: topic alignment PN = mean of Purity and NMI
baselines: 8 NTMs as base models (e.g. NVDM, ProdLDA, SCHOLAR, ETM, NSTM, ECRTM)
key_results: C_V improves for every base NTM, from +7.4% (NSTM on DBpedia) to +70.6% (ECRTM on 20News).
Topic alignment stays comparable to the base model, changing between -3.5% and +4.2%.
Example: ETM on 20News, C_V 0.491 -> 0.578 with LLM-ITL.
strengths: Model-agnostic: works with many NTMs and LLMs.
LLM is queried at the word level, cheaper than document-level LLM topic modelling.
Keeps document-topic proportions, which TopicGPT does not provide.
Confidence weighting reduces the effect of LLM hallucination on hard topics.

limitations.text: Over-reliance on the LLM can inject out-of-corpus information or bias topics toward the LLM's pre-training knowledge, hurting alignment when the corpus differs from the LLM's training data.
Each trial takes a few hours on a single 80GB A100 GPU.

notes: Five runs with different seeds; mean and std reported.
